newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end mixed, March T-bond lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end mixed, March T-bond lower.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended mixed, with March T-bonds lower after failing to pierce intraday resistance late.

March cut losses and climbed a few ticks shy of the day's session high late, but was thwarted by stiff resistance at 111-16/32 to 18/32, said Don Pullen, bond trading floor manager for ED&F Man. March reached a session high at 111-18/32 early in the day, surpassing Tuesday's high of 111-15/32, but reached only 111-14/32 on the late rally.
"I think we built up resistance from this morning that we just couldn't get through," Pullen said.
Pullen said strength in crude oil attracted traders' attention late, as well.
The short end and notes futures all ended in positive territory, though traders said action there was alternately choppy and thin.
June Eurodollars, which took over lead contract status from March, finished steady at 94.19. Traders pegged key support in June at 94.18-20 and resistance at 94.26.
March 10-year notes sparked the late rise from session lows as one dealer reportedly bought 3,000 March note contracts just after midday.

Traders cited scant reaction to November business inventories, reported up 0.1 percent after an 0.5-percent rise in October. Wall Street economists had expected inventories to rise 0.3 percent in November.
Traders said traders were disappointed early in the day that March T-bonds failed to get higher than 111-15/32 on Tuesday.
"Shorts are jittery and ready to cover at the drop of a hat," said Mike Boss, futures analyst with Aubrey Lanston.
Indeed, many traders said the near-term outlook was confusing after March T-bond's behavior since Friday.
March collapsed to the lowest price since October on Friday, was stagnant on Monday and rallied a point on Tuesday. Wednesday's market action was deemed choppy and consolidative.
Technicians said March could be in for range trade between 110-00 and 112-00.
At settlement, March T-bonds were down 4/32 to 111-9/32, T-notes were flat at 108-17/32, muni-bonds lost 5/32 to 114-29/32 and T-bills rose two bps to 94.92.
